programmes.d: Tracy Rattigan, the show's guest host while Alan Brady is on vacation, is a charming but incorrigible flirt.
Rob finds himself caught in the middle after Buddy announces he is going to divorce Pickles.
Laura's old flame re-enters the Petries' lives as Alan Brady's newest sponsor.
Rob drives himself beyond distraction trying to figure out whether Laura is going to throw him a surprise party for his birthday.
Carter and an old war buddy credit each other for being war heroes.
Duke talks Gomer into taking a jeep to the airport.
Gomer is a look-out for burglars robbing the base.
Gomer gets assigned to MP duty.
Carter wants his men to pass a promotion test.
Gomer holds a wedding ring for a friend and it appears to be lost when they spend a night baking bread.
Hogan goes to the hospital to get information from a wounded contact.
Hogan has a touchy mission to deliver ammunition to the underground.
The Germans are sending Hogan to America demanding surrender along with another surprise.
A glamorous English woman defects to the enemy and designs a super-effective aircraft defense system.
An Italian officer helps Hogan photograph a new German anti-aircraft gun.
For Colonel Hogan's birthday his crew decides to give him one ammunition dump freshly destroyed.

The Douglases are offered a free paint job on their house and barn so long as they allow the paint company free advertising on their barn wall. Meanwhile, Lisa tries to make spaghetti for Oliver's upcoming birthday. Will it prove im-pasta-ble?

While staying with the Douglases, Arnold the Pig witnesses a bank robbery when he goes with the Douglases on an errand in Pixley. When Lisa asks him to describe the two robbers, Arnold, reliving the moment, loses his voice from fear.

Oliver refuses to take Lisa to the annual Carpenter's Ball because he thinks the attendees are too eccentric for his liking. But Lisa has her own motives to attend. She is trying to get a romance sparked between two local singles.

Aloha! The Douglases vacation in Hawaii. But the daughter of the hotel manager needs to keep secret that she double booked the honeymoon suite. The 'sweet' surprise? While Lisa and Oliver settle in, they are unaware that the other room is occupied.

Oliver's heirloom watch is broken so he tries to find his ex-secretary Carol's address to ask her the name of the jeweler who fixed it last time. Carol is now working and living in Los Angeles, and we get a glimpse into her new life.

When Oliver decides to attend night school and enrolls in a farming class, Lisa does the same, taking psychology. Before long, many of the residents of Hooterville are lining up for appointments with the eminent Dr. Lisa.
Steve's Chinese friend invites Chip to a birthday party.
Mike falls for an older woman.
Steve takes the boys along for a business trip to Rome.

It's Christmas Day and Archie is the only one not in the Christmas spirit. Mike and Gloria question him, but he refuses to reveal what's bugging him. The Jeffersons come over to wish the Bunkers a 'Merry Christmas'.

Archie comes home from work in a great mood and orders Edith to have dinner ready and waiting, because he has to watch the CBS Evening News to see himself on it. Archie was interviewed as a man-on-the-street voicing his opinions on Nixon's presidency.

Edith has been running herself ragged caring for Archie, Mike and Gloria, who have all come down with a terrible flu. This prompts her to call on her extremely liberal Cousin Maude to come and stay with the Bunkers and help out.

Archie, Mike and Gloria are stunned when Edith becomes a rollercoaster of moods, going from joy to anger to tears in a snap of a finger. Gloria sits her down and suggests that perhaps she's beginning menopause.
Arthur is determined to teach his visiting grandson the important things in life, but it's the guilty grandpa who learns the most valuable lesson of all.

When Victoria Butterfield's self-righteous father comes to take her away from the 'permissive' Findlay household, Maude confronts him with his less-than-honorable secret. Roscoe Lee Browne returns in the guest star role of Mr. Butterfield.
Maude's grandson Phillip is devastated when he finally finds out the real reason why an 'older woman' has been dating him.

Maude plans a dinner party for her friend, U.S. Congresswoman MacIlhaney, and then plans a new job as her assistant. But Maude could never plan on what's yet to come in the first episode of a three-part story.
Maude mourns the moving of her dearest friends the Harmons until the death of someone close has a drastic effect on her mood...and her life...on the second of a three-part episode.
Sparks start flying when the newly appointed U.S. Congresswoman Maude Findlay arrives in Washington D.C., throwing a monkey wrench into the political machinery by insisting upon doing things her way.
Elaine becomes a nervous wreck when her young son decides to give up the oboe and take up boxing under the tutelage of Tony.
When Jim's old girlfriend shows up hoping to rekindle their romance, Alex quickly sets out to win her heart away from her former suitor.
On the eve of the biggest fight of his career, Tony loses interest in boxing when his girlfriend announces she may be expecting his baby.
Louie is worried his blind girlfriend will no longer love him if an operation to restore her sight is successful.
Felix gets Oscar in trouble with the Internal Revenue Service.
To raise funds for his financially troubled amateur opera club, Felix induces Oscar to arrange for a gambling event.
Felix and Oscar are arrested and charged with ticket scalping.
After burning a hole in Felix's bed, Oscar despairs of raising the money for a new one. But a poker session with his old college friend, Monty Hall, leads to an idea.
Billie Joe receives an endowment, but instead of using it for medical school, she wishes to go to Hollywood.
Kate tries to convince Billie Jo that she is sick in order to set her up with Dr. Harris.
A big movie star stays at Shady Rest.
Uncle Joe tries to convince two rich women that Shady Rest is a farm.
